comparison.objective: Diagnose a faulty cable core by simultaneously cranking an insulation tester and probing three studs, then mark the failed core. Candidate commissions a mechanical axis damper through adjustment and repeated impact trials.
comparison.physical_skill: Record requires sustained bimanual crank-and-probe contact, sequential testing, diagnosis, flag actuation, and probe replacement. Candidate requires hex-key engagement, counterholding, unlocking, fine collar rotation, torque-limited relocking, and response-guided iteration.
comparison.success_condition: Record requires all three 1 s tests at ≥0.4 rev/s, only the faulty flag red, probe returned, hands clear, and stillness. Candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J physical cycles within stroke and velocity limits after relocking, with no hard-stop strike or setting drift.
comparison.reason: Both involve bimanual manipulation and feedback, but one tests electrical fault diagnosis under continuous cranking while the other tests mechanical commissioning and retention under dynamic impacts. Candidate still lacks numeric definitions for excessive rebound, overload, collar-drift tolerance, and witness torque; those omissions do not make these objectives plausible duplicates.
